headline.note: The pre-parliament record includes two overlapping retail jobs and a company directorship, but no source establishes substantive full-time hours or exact work dates. Political staff, nonprofit advocacy, union work and elected office are excluded categories. Missing evidence is not zero.

career_spells.evidence_note: The NSW Parliament biography identifies the employer and 1982–1987 years, refining the frozen biography's combined 1982–1991 sales/shop-assistant entry. Burke was aged about 12 at commencement; hours, pay, school-term pattern and exact dates are unresolved. Inaugural speech identifies Sunday deliveries, initially10% sales commission later12.5%, and a six-year recollection. Supports paid work, not a full-time roster; original year endpoints retained without age-based recalculation.

career_spells.evidence_note: The NSW Parliament biography identifies Grace Bros Roselands and 1985–1991, overlapping newsagency work through 1987 and university study. Hours, leave and exact dates are unresolved. First speech describes supplementary work begun at15; not enough to establish formal casual/part-time status or weekly hours. Follow-up2026-10-02:16November2022 first-person address explicitly calls his Grace Brothers job casual, resolving contractual-status gap. His associated recollection describes Thursday-night/Saturday casual rostering, not a quantified individual roster throughout1985–1991. Schema has no casual enum; employment_status remains unknown as to substantive full-time/part-time hours. No FTE inferred.
